description: A black liquid has brought down prime ministers, started wars and enriched empires. Here's why **oil** is never just energy.

hero.hook: For a century, whoever controls oil has controlled a share of world power.

blocks.text: **oil** is not a simple source of energy. It is the resource that has most shaped global geopolitics for a century, and which continues to weigh on the balance of power today.

Its energy density and ease of transport made it the engine of the industrial revolution, but also the trigger of crises and wars. Understanding oil means understanding why some countries became so rich, and why others fought wars for its control.

The era of industrial oil began in 1859, when American engineer Edwin Drake drilled the first commercial well in Pennsylvania. But it was prospecting in the Middle East that really changed the map of power: Iran in 1908, Iraq in 1927, then Saudi Arabia and Kuwait in 1938.
Before becoming a fuel, Pennsylvania oil was sold in bottles as a miracle cure believed to cure both rheumatism and baldness.

For decades, this wealth was exploited by a group of Western companies nicknamed the “Seven Sisters”, who imposed very disadvantageous contracts and kept control of prices. This domination creates a frustration which prepares a future claim for sovereignty.

sections.title: The awakening of black gold, from Pennsylvania to the Gulf

blocks.text: Faced with this domination, five producing countries founded the **OPEC** in 1960 in Baghdad, to regain control of their resources and stabilize prices. But this wealth does not always bring the expected prosperity: it is the , when the abundance of hydrocarbons stifles other sectors and favors authoritarian regimes. **[[Resource curse (The)]]**

The breaking point came during the oil shock of 1973. In the middle of , the Arab countries of OPEC decreed an embargo against Israel's allies. In six months, the price of a barrel has quadrupled. **[[Yom Kippur War]]**

blocks.caption: The oil crisis of 1973 caused long lines at gas stations across the Western world.

blocks.text: Western economies, dependent on this continuous flow, are plunging into a crisis combining high inflation and stagnant growth, forcing States to rethink their energy security.

sections.title: The birth of OPEC and the oil weapon

blocks.text: Oil became central to most of the major conflicts of the late 20th century. One of the earliest examples was Iranian Prime Minister 's attempt to nationalize British oil companies in 1951, before being overthrown in 1953 by a Western coup. **[[Mohammad Mossadegh]]**

The Persian Gulf is becoming the epicenter of chronic instability. In 1990, Iraq's invasion of Kuwait directly threatened the global market. The 1991 Gulf War was as much about freeing a sovereign state as it was about preventing Iraq from controlling a huge share of the world's reserves.
During the 1991 Gulf War, oil well fires set by the Iraqi army were so large they were visible from space and caused local temperatures to drop several degrees.

The same scenario is repeated with the Iraq war of 2003. Today, this dynamic is moving towards civil wars: in Venezuela, Nigeria or Libya, control of wells and refineries remains the nerve of internal struggles, because whoever owns the oil has the means to finance their army.

At the turn of the 2010s, oil geopolitics experienced a real technical earthquake. Thanks to hydraulic fracturing, the United States is massively exploiting . This shift allows them to become the world's leading producer, reducing their historical dependence on the Middle East. **[[shale oil]]**

This new abundance has for a time made us forget the fears linked to peak oil, the theory which predicts an inevitable end of the resource. But if the supply has diversified, tensions have not disappeared: they are moving towards transport routes, such as the Strait of Hormuz, or towards new contested deposits in the eastern Mediterranean.

The oil shock of 1973, by quadrupling the price of a barrel after the Arab embargo, transformed hydrocarbons into a major geopolitical weapon and revealed the vulnerability of developed countries in the face of their energy dependence.
